reviews.protects: the synchronous save path is atomic too: a failure keeps the old file.

reviews.protects: a destination near the 255-character component limit still publishes, on both the asynchronous and synchronous paths, new and existing (on Windows the full path is over MAX_PATH, so the raw Win32 calls need the verbatim form).

reviews.protects: staging names are short, independent of the destination, unique per call and live next to the destination.
reviews.detects: a name that embeds the destination basename or repeats between calls.

reviews.protects: shutdown during an in-flight load is final: the finished model is discarded (outside the slot lock) and nothing is loaded afterwards.
reviews.detects: an unconditional install after load (the pre-fix behaviour), or a stale model freed while the slot lock is held.
reviews.needs: no model; the paused load is a closure blocked on a channel.

reviews.protects: the reverse ordering still works: shutdown, then a new load, installs normally, and replacing a model frees the old one outside the lock.
reviews.detects: an epoch check that rejects every load after the first shutdown.
reviews.needs: no model.

reviews.protects: a load queued behind a running generation is cancelled when shutdown runs first: it never reaches the loader and the slot stays empty.
reviews.detects: capturing the lifecycle epoch after the gate is held (the load then adopts the post-shutdown epoch and installs a model after shutdown), or dropping the stale check that runs before any weights are read.
reviews.needs: no model; the generation is the test holding the gate.

reviews.protects: a load admitted after shutdown installs normally, even while a generation still holds the gate when shutdown ran.
reviews.detects: a stale check that rejects every load once any shutdown has happened.
reviews.needs: no model.

reviews.protects: the exported load path is wired to the lifecycle: a pcai_media_load_model style request queued behind a generation, then shutdown, reports ModelNotLoaded and never tries to read the (nonexistent) model path.
reviews.detects: load_model_at taking the gate itself before admission, or passing the wrong slot or gate, which would surface as an I/O error for the missing path.
reviews.needs: no model; the path does not exist, so reaching the loader would fail loudly.

reviews.protects: a failed load leaves the slot, and the epoch, alone.
reviews.detects: an error path that clears a previously loaded model.
reviews.needs: no model.

reviews.protects: the exported pcai_media_shutdown invalidates in-flight loads of the real global slot (not just the generic helper).
reviews.detects: shutdown that stops touching MODEL_SLOT, or only clears the handle without bumping the epoch.
reviews.needs: no model.

reviews.protects: a publish on slow or stalled storage blocks nobody else: poll and cancel of other requests answer within 100 ms while one request sits in its rename.
reviews.detects: the rename (or any file IO) running under the global request-table lock.
reviews.needs: no model; the rename is a mock publish step blocked on a channel.

reviews.protects: a failing rename while publishing reports Failed, removes the staging file and leaves the destination alone, again without the global lock.
reviews.detects: an error path that leaves the request Publishing or leaks the partial file.
reviews.needs: a temp directory; the publish step is a mock that fails.

reviews.protects: replacing an existing output keeps its access mode on the sync and the async path: a private 0600 file stays 0600 and a 0640 file stays 0640.
reviews.detects: a staged file that keeps its own default mode (0644 under umask 022) after the rename, which would expose a private image, or one forced to a fixed mode.
reviews.needs: Unix; the umask is set to 022 so a default-mode staging file would be 0644.

reviews.protects: the staging file is private (0600) for as long as it exists, so a half-written image is never readable by other users.
reviews.detects: a staging file created with the default mode (0644 under umask 022).
reviews.needs: Unix; the encoder stats the open staging file, so no extra seam is needed.

reviews.protects: a brand-new output gets the mode a plain File::create would have given it (0666 filtered by the umask), not the private staging mode and not a wider one.
reviews.detects: a new file left at the private 0600 staging mode, or opened up beyond the umask.
reviews.needs: Unix; sets the umask explicitly (027 and 077) and restores it.

reviews.protects: a failure while preparing the publish (here the staging file vanishes before the permission copy) reports Failed, leaves the existing destination untouched and leaves no staging file.
reviews.detects: publish errors that are swallowed, or a destination replaced or truncated despite the failure.
reviews.needs: nothing platform specific; the real publish_staged runs after the staging file is removed, which makes both the Unix permission copy and Windows ReplaceFileW fail.

reviews.protects: replacing an existing file whose ACL was explicitly restricted keeps that ACL (ReplaceFileW merges it) instead of leaving the new file with the directory's inherited ACL.
reviews.detects: a plain rename of the staged file over the destination.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; the test restricts its own temp file only.

reviews.protects: replacing an existing output keeps its owning group, so a 0640 file is not handed to a different group when its mode bits are preserved.
reviews.detects: a publish that copies the mode but leaves the staged file in the process's own group, on the sync and the async path.
reviews.needs: Unix and a second group this process may use (any group as root); the test returns early with a message when there is none, so its positive control is the mutation that skips the group copy.

reviews.protects: a destination with a POSIX access ACL is not silently replaced by a file that has lost it: the publish is refused with an explicit error, the destination keeps its bytes, mode and ACL, and no staging file is left.
reviews.detects: an ACL-blind publish that widens access, or one that reports success.
reviews.needs: Linux and a filesystem with POSIX ACL xattrs; returns early with a message when the xattr cannot be set.  After a successful setxattr the test reads the xattr back, so a passing run proves the ACL was really present.

reviews.protects: the staging file is never readable by other users while it exists: its DACL is protected (no inherited entries) and names only the owner and SYSTEM.
reviews.detects: a staging file that inherits the directory's ACL, which would expose a half-written image during encoding even when the destination is restricted.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; reads the staging ACL before any publish.

reviews.protects: a failure to carry the destination's ACL onto the replacement is an error, not a silent success that publishes the directory's inherited ACL.
reviews.detects: ReplaceFileW called with REPLACEFILE_IGNORE_MERGE_ERRORS.  The merge is made to fail by denying WRITE_DAC on the staged file.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH.

reviews.protects: a brand-new output gets the directory's inherited ACL, exactly what a plain File::create would have produced, not the private staging ACL.
reviews.detects: a new file left owner/SYSTEM-only after the rename.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH.

reviews.protects: when the replace step fails (for example the merge of the destination's ACL), the request is Failed, the destination keeps its bytes and ACL, and the staging file is removed; nothing is published.
reviews.detects: a publish that swallows the replace error, falls back to a plain rename, or leaves the staging file behind.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; the failure is injected through the replace seam.

reviews.protects: when preserving the destination's access control fails (group copy, ACL check or mode copy), the request is Failed, the destination keeps its bytes and mode, and the staging file is removed; nothing is published.
reviews.detects: a publish that goes ahead after the preservation step reported an error.
reviews.needs: Unix; the failure is injected through the preserve seam.

reviews.protects: a successful publish over an existing destination keeps its ACL and leaves neither the ReplaceFileW backup nor the staging file behind.
reviews.detects: a publish that forgets to delete the backup (the user's previous image would linger as a hidden `.pcai-*.bak` file), or one that leaks the staging file.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; the real ReplaceFileW runs.

reviews.protects: `replace_file_keeping_acl` really passes the backup name to ReplaceFileW, so Windows keeps the original under that name while it swaps; the failure paths below can only restore from a backup that exists.
reviews.detects: a null `lpBackupFileName`: with it ERROR_UNABLE_TO_MOVE_REPLACEMENT (1176) deletes the user's image and nothing can bring it back.
reviews.needs: Windows; calls the real ReplaceFileW on throwaway files.

reviews.protects: ERROR_UNABLE_TO_MOVE_REPLACEMENT (1176) with a backup requested.  Microsoft Learn (ReplaceFileW, return value): "If lpBackupFileName was specified, the replaced and replacement files retain their original file names."  So the destination is still the original and no backup exists; the restore must be a no-op that does not touch the destination, the request is Failed, and the staging file is removed.
reviews.detects: a restore that moves or deletes something when nothing was moved aside, or a publish that reports the failure as success.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; the documented file state is injected through the replace seam (nothing is moved).

reviews.protects: ERROR_UNABLE_TO_MOVE_REPLACEMENT_2 (1177).  Microsoft Learn: "The replacement file still exists under its original name ... The file to be replaced still exists with a different name. If lpBackupFileName is specified, it will be the name of the replaced file."  So the original is at the backup name and the destination name is free: the original is moved back (without replacing), the staging file is removed, the request is Failed, and no backup is left.
reviews.detects: a publish that leaves the original at the backup name, or one that deletes the backup before restoring it.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; the documented file state is injected through the replace seam.

reviews.protects: any other ReplaceFileW failure (the documented rule is that the files keep their names and no backup exists) leaves the destination as it was, with no backup name left over; nothing is "restored" from a backup that was never made.
reviews.detects: a publish that treats a missing backup as an error of its own, or that moves or deletes the destination while cleaning up.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; the failure is injected through the replace seam.

reviews.protects: when the restore itself fails, the backup is kept (it is the user's only copy) and the error names its path, so the original can be recovered by hand.
reviews.detects: a publish that deletes the backup after a failed restore, or reports the failure without the backup's location.
reviews.needs: Windows; the failure state is injected through the replace seam and the move is made to fail for real by putting a directory under the destination name, which a file cannot replace.  (Holding the backup open instead would also block deleting it, so the test could not tell "kept" from "could not delete".)

reviews.protects: the no-replace move fills a free name and, when the name is occupied, fails with AlreadyExists and leaves both the destination and the staged file exactly as they were.
reviews.detects: a replacing rename on the new-output path: a file that appears after the existence check would be overwritten.
reviews.needs: Unix or Windows; plain files in a temporary directory.

reviews.protects: the hard-link fallback (used where `renameat2` is unavailable) has the same contract as the primary no-replace move.
reviews.detects: a fallback that overwrites, or that leaves the staging name behind.
reviews.needs: Unix on a filesystem with hard links (a temporary directory).

reviews.protects: a file that appears at a new output's path between the existence check and the publish is not overwritten: the request is Failed with an explicit error, the file keeps its bytes and ACL, and the staging file is removed.
reviews.detects: a replacing rename after "not found" (the other process's private file would be clobbered by the generated image).
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; the appearance is injected through the metadata seam, which reports "not found" and then creates the file.

reviews.protects: a metadata error other than "not found" (here access denied) is not read as "the destination is absent": the publish fails closed with that error, the existing destination keeps its bytes and ACL, and the staging file is removed.
reviews.detects: a check that treats every metadata error as absence and then publishes over a file it could not see.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; the error is injected through the metadata seam.

reviews.protects: as the Windows test of the same name, on Unix: a file that appears at a new output's path after the check is not overwritten; the request is Failed with an explicit error, the file keeps its bytes and mode, and the staging file is removed.
reviews.detects: a replacing rename after "not found".
reviews.needs: Unix; the appearance is injected through the metadata seam.

reviews.protects: as the Windows test of the same name, on Unix: a metadata error other than "not found" fails the publish closed, before the access-control step runs.
reviews.detects: a check that treats every metadata error as absence.
reviews.needs: Unix; the error is injected through the metadata seam.

reviews.protects: a regular file that appears at the destination while a failed replace is being undone belongs to another writer and is never overwritten by the restore: the request is Failed, the concurrent file keeps its bytes and ACL, the backup is kept, and the error names the backup and says the destination exists.
reviews.detects: a restore with a replacing rename (MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING), which would clobber the concurrent file with the original.
reviews.needs: Windows with icacls on PATH; the 1177 state is injected through the replace seam, which then creates the concurrent file at the free destination name.

reviews.protects: one probe decides "new or existing" for the permission policy AND the publication primitive.  A target that is removed after the probe (here: after the access-control step) is not published as a replacement: the request is Failed with an explicit error, the destination is not created, and the staging file is removed.
reviews.detects: a flow that re-probes in the access-control step and then renames over (or into) whatever is there, applying existing-file semantics to a file that is gone.
reviews.needs: Unix; the removal is injected through the preserve seam after the real step.

reviews.protects: the decision made from the probe is the only one: when the probe reports an existing file that the access-control step then cannot find, the publish fails closed instead of switching to new-file permissions and a replacing rename.
reviews.detects: an access-control step that probes the destination again and disagrees with the first decision.
reviews.needs: Unix; the stale probe result is injected through the metadata seam (it reports another, existing file for a destination that is absent).

reviews.protects: the access ACL a staging file inherits from a directory's DEFAULT ACL is removed by the access-control step before the destination's mode is copied, so the mode copy cannot raise the ACL mask and activate the inherited named entry.
reviews.detects: a missing or misplaced strip (the staged file would keep the named user's entry, effective at the copied 0640).
reviews.needs: Linux and a filesystem with POSIX ACL xattrs; returns early with a message when the default ACL cannot be set.  Positive control: the staging file really carries an inherited access ACL before the step runs.

reviews.protects: a destination with plain mode bits (0640, no ACL) in a directory that has a DEFAULT ACL with a named user entry is replaced without gaining an access ACL, on the synchronous and the asynchronous path.  The staging file inherits the default ACL with its named entry masked by the 0600 mode; copying the destination's 0640 would raise the mask and make that entry effective, widening access to the image.
reviews.detects: a publish that copies the mode but leaves the inherited access ACL on the staged file (the published image would then be readable by the named user).
reviews.needs: Linux and a filesystem with POSIX ACL xattrs; returns early with a message when the default ACL cannot be set.  A positive control creates a probe file and requires it to carry an inherited access ACL, so a passing run proves the directory's default ACL was operative.

reviews.protects: a directory that takes the destination's name after validation is never swapped out of place: the request is Failed, the directory and its contents are still at the destination path, and the staging file is removed.  The destination is re-checked just before a plain rename, and the kernel would refuse the rename of a file over a directory anyway.
reviews.detects: a publish that skips the re-check and reports a different outcome than the explicit "changed" refusal (here the kernel's EISDIR, with no custody message).
reviews.needs: Linux; the substitution is injected between the validation and the publish.

reviews.protects: a different regular file that replaces the validated one (another writer, new inode) is not displaced either: Failed, that file is back at the destination with its bytes, and the staging file is removed.
reviews.detects: a re-check that looks only at the file type, not the identity (dev and inode) recorded at validation: a plain rename would replace the other writer's file.
reviews.needs: Linux; the substitute is created under another name first and renamed over the destination, so it cannot reuse the old inode number.

reviews.protects: a symlink that replaces the destination after validation is neither followed nor replaced: Failed, the symlink is still at the destination path and still points at its target, whose bytes are untouched.
reviews.detects: a re-check that lets a symlink through (a plain rename replaces the link itself), or a publish that writes through the link.
reviews.needs: Linux; the substitution is injected between validation and publish.

reviews.protects: a destination that already is a symlink is refused, not followed and not replaced: the publish returns an explicit error, the link and its target are untouched and no staging file is left.  (The destination is classified with `symlink_metadata`, so a link is never mistaken for the regular file behind it.)
reviews.detects: a publish that follows the link, or replaces the link with a regular file and reports success.
reviews.needs: Unix.

reviews.protects: when `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` is unsupported, the no-replace move uses `link` followed by `unlink`, which is atomic and never overwrites: a free name is filled and the staging name removed; an occupied one is refused with "not overwritten" and both files are untouched.
reviews.detects: a fallback that checks and then renames (a vanished path could be recreated in the gap), or one that overwrites.
reviews.needs: Unix on a filesystem with hard links (a temporary directory); the unsupported primitive is injected.

reviews.protects: where neither `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` nor hard links are available the publish fails closed with an explicit error instead of falling back to a check followed by a rename: nothing is published and the staged file is untouched.
reviews.detects: a fallback that renames when it cannot link.
reviews.needs: Unix; both primitives are injected as unsupported.

reviews.protects: cleanup after a failed publish deletes the staging path only while it still holds the file this process created, and does nothing if it is already gone.
reviews.detects: a cleanup that leaves our own staging file behind, or that reports a problem where there is none.
reviews.needs: Unix or Windows (file identity is read from the OS); no global state.

reviews.protects: if something other than the generated file is at the staging path (another writer renamed a file over it), cleanup never deletes it: the file is moved to a `.pcai-<hex>.rescued` name beside it, with its bytes, and the note names that path.
reviews.detects: a cleanup that unlinks by path (the other writer's data would be lost), or that drops the identity comparison, or that skips the rescue.
reviews.needs: Unix or Windows; no global state.

reviews.protects: if the rescue itself fails, the file that is not ours is left exactly where it is (never deleted) and the note names the staging path.
reviews.detects: a cleanup that unlinks after a failed rescue.
reviews.needs: Unix or Windows; the rescue failure is injected; no global state.

reviews.protects: on the asynchronous path, a publish that fails after another writer has put a file at the staging path does not delete it: the request is Failed, the error names the `.rescued` file, which holds the other writer's bytes, and the destination keeps its own bytes.
reviews.detects: a caller that unlinks the staging path on any error.
reviews.needs: Unix or Windows; the failure and the foreign file are injected through the publish seam.

reviews.protects: the same on the synchronous path.
reviews.detects: a caller that unlinks the staging path on any error.
reviews.needs: Unix or Windows; the failure and the foreign file are injected through the publish seam.

reviews.protects: every test that touches the process-wide FFI state takes the serial guard, so libtest's parallel threads cannot race on the lifecycle epoch, the model slot, the inference gate or the request table.
reviews.detects: a new or edited test that calls an exported entry point, the state mutex, the slot or the gate (directly or through a helper) without `serialize_global_state()`; the dropped guard otherwise surfaces only as an intermittent failure under plain `cargo test`, which nextest hides.
reviews.needs: nothing but this file's own source (read with include_str!).

reviews.protects: the metadata probe describes 7B tensor shapes without allocating them.
reviews.detects: a probe that materializes real payloads (tens of GiB) or answers presence queries as true.
reviews.needs: CPU only; one scalar tensor.

reviews.protects: the derived 7B required-tensor schema keeps every generation component and drops the aligner and GGUF backbone.
reviews.detects: constructor changes that silently remove a required tensor from the preflight, or leak optional ones into it.
reviews.needs: CPU only; constructor metadata, no weights.

reviews.protects: invalid head counts fail as an error instead of a divide-by-zero or a wrong schema.
reviews.detects: removal of the divisibility guards in required_generation_metadata.
reviews.needs: CPU only.

reviews.protects: a nonempty but incomplete 7B checkpoint is refused before the VarMap or GGUF is touched, in both load modes.
reviews.detects: a preflight that is skipped or reordered after allocation (this would try to allocate a 7B model).
reviews.needs: temp directory; no model download, GPU or GGUF file.

reviews.protects: a model directory holding only PyTorch weights is refused with the exact conversion command for that directory, not a bare "no shards" message.
reviews.detects: the refusal losing its preparation guidance, or load proceeding to allocate.
reviews.needs: a temp directory only; no model, GPU or network.

reviews.protects: generation-only checkpoints load while understanding stays unavailable.
reviews.detects: treating a missing vision tower or aligner as a fatal generation error, or as loaded.
reviews.needs: CPU only; tiny safetensors fixture.

reviews.protects: aligner readiness is reported true only when every aligner tensor is present.
reviews.detects: a partial aligner being reported as ready (random aligner weights would then reach understanding).
reviews.needs: CPU only; tiny safetensors fixture.

reviews.protects: a checkpoint with only aligner tensors cannot pass as a generation checkpoint.
reviews.detects: optional components masking missing required generation tensors.
reviews.needs: CPU only; tiny safetensors fixture.

reviews.protects: a model directory with no safetensors shards fails for both safetensors and GGUF loads.
reviews.detects: the old behaviour of warning and running with random weights.
